turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Honestly, I don’t really see the point of talking about it—people make too much fuss. I’ve been feeling pretty apathetic, and lately I’ve had strong cravings for chocolate pudding and potato chips, which has led to a lot of weight gain.
How long have you been experiencing these cravings and weight gain, and have you noticed any other changes in your body or mood during this time?

“About six months now, give or take—I’ve also gotten more unkempt and I don’t really engage with my family the way I used to. My mood feels pretty blunted, and at times I’ve made inappropriate comments and tried to initiate physical contact with strangers, which I know isn’t appropriate.”
Have you noticed any problems with your memory for recent events, or would you say your memory is relatively normal while these behavioral and personality changes are the main issue?

“I wouldn’t say my memory is noticeably bad for recent events—I can recall things well enough. It’s more that my behavior and mood feel off, with blunted affect and that shift toward inappropriate comments and physical contact attempts, plus the strong cravings and weight gain.”
How old are you, and have you noticed any changes in your speech or language abilities, or any new physical symptoms like weakness, stiffness, or tremors?
“I’m 55, and my speech seems about the same to me—no new slurring or trouble finding words. I haven’t noticed weakness, stiffness, or tremors; it’s mainly the change in how I act and feel.”
Have you developed any repetitive behaviors, compulsive rituals, or unusual preoccupations with certain activities or objects during these past six months?

“I don’t have specific rituals, but I do get fixated on having chocolate pudding and potato chips, and it feels hard to ignore that pull. Other than that, I’ve mostly just noticed my apathy and how my comments and behavior have become inappropriate without much control.”
Do you feel like you can understand and share the feelings of your family members the same way you used to, or do you find yourself feeling indifferent to their emotions?

“I feel pretty indifferent to my family’s emotions now—I don’t really connect with them the way I used to, and I’m not very interested in their feelings. It doesn’t seem to bother me much, and I mostly keep my focus on those cravings and my own thoughts. I’m not sure I’d say I can share their feelings like before.”
Have you noticed any changes in your walking pattern, balance, or urinary control (like urgency or accidents)?

“I haven’t noticed any changes in how I walk or my balance, and I haven’t had any urinary urgency or accidents. It’s mainly been my apathy, blunted affect, disinterest in my family, and those intense cravings alongside the inappropriate comments.”
[DDX] Behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia, Major Depressive Disorder, Late-onset Bipolar Disorder/Mania, Frontal Lobe Neoplasm, Neurosyphilis
